Adjusted summary incorporating April 2025 Beige Book and SLOOS insights:
- Policy: FOMC holds at 4.25–4.50 percent and continues balance‑sheet runoff; emphasizes data dependence and elevated two‑sided risks (higher unemployment and higher inflation risks both have risen).
- Beige Book (mid‑April 2025, prepared by the Atlanta Fed): On balance, activity was little changed to slightly up. Consumer spending was mixed with softer discretionary goods and more price sensitivity; travel/leisure remained steady. Labor markets eased modestly with improved applicant availability and slower wage growth; firms reported reduced pricing power and more discounting as input cost pressures moderated. Manufacturing was mixed; residential real estate showed pockets of stabilization amid tight inventory; CRE—especially office—remained weak. Several districts noted tighter credit availability and weaker loan demand.
- Inflation: Still somewhat elevated, but Beige Book anecdotes point to moderating price pressures and waning pass‑through.
- SLOOS read‑through: Weaker C&I and CRE loan demand; further tightening in standards (notably outside large banks). Drivers include a softer outlook and lower risk tolerance. This implies tighter credit supply and softer loan demand—a drag on future activity that should aid disinflation but raises downside risk to growth and employment.
- Financial stability overlay: Elevated asset valuations, ongoing CRE stress, and some rise in consumer delinquencies, offset by resilient core banking and well‑functioning Treasury markets.

Net: Beige Book corroborates SLOOS signals of softening demand, easing wage/price pressures, and tighter credit. This tempers the statement’s “solid pace” characterization and tilts the overall assessment modestly negative versus the prior near‑neutral read.
